title: Webhook endpoints fully exempt from rate limiting — no DoS protection
description: The @fastify/rate-limit allowList callback passes any URL starting with /api/v1/payments/webhooks/ through without any rate limit. Every request triggers HMAC verification, DB dedup lookup, and potentially notification queue writes. An attacker can flood the endpoint and exhaust the DB connection pool.
root_cause: app.ts:119 uses allowList to exempt the entire /api/v1/payments/webhooks/* path, including the :provider path parameter. No per-IP or per-source rate limit is applied as a fallback.
intended_behavior: Rate limiting should protect the webhook endpoint against floods while still allowing legitimate provider retry bursts.

trace.description: Public webhook entry point — no auth required, provider path param is unbounded
Any URL starting with /api/v1/payments/webhooks/ bypasses global 120/min rate limiter
HMAC computation + DB write executed on every request with no rate gate

evidence.description: allowList: (request) => request.url.startsWith('/api/v1/payments/webhooks/') — completely removes rate limiting from all webhook URLs
config: { rateLimit: false } on the webhook route also disables per-route limiting

conditions.description: Attacker must be able to reach the backend API (not behind strict IP allowlist for webhook endpoints)

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated external caller who can send HTTP POST requests to the API
payloads: POST /api/v1/payments/webhooks/razorpay with arbitrary body, repeated at high rate
instructions: Send continuous POST requests to /api/v1/payments/webhooks/razorpay with any JSON body
Observe that requests are not rate-limited — all receive 401 (invalid signature) but consume server resources
At high volume, DB connection pool becomes exhausted and other API requests start failing
execution.observed_result: No rate limiting enforced. Each request performs HMAC verification and DB lookup regardless of signature validity.

remediation.strategy: Apply a per-source-IP rate limit using keyGenerator on the webhook endpoint rather than exempting it entirely. A limit of 300-500 requests per minute per IP accommodates legitimate provider retry bursts while blocking sustained floods.

likelihood.reason: Requires network access to the backend. Production deployment on Render may have upstream rate limiting from CDN/load balancer that provides partial protection.

impact.reason: Can cause availability degradation and connection pool exhaustion for other API users. Does not directly expose data or allow privilege escalation.

confidence.reason: Rate limit exemption is directly observable in source at app.ts:119 and payment.routes.ts:17. No deployment-visible fact changes this assessment.

title: Timing-Allow-Origin: * on all API responses enables cross-origin timing side-channel
description: The networkHeaders middleware sets Timing-Allow-Origin: * on every API response. This overrides the browser same-origin policy for the Resource Timing API, allowing any cross-origin page to precisely measure response times for API requests made by a victim's browser. Enables existence timing for booking IDs and admin session validity probes.
root_cause: networkHeaders.ts sets the header unconditionally with a wildcard value rather than restricting to the application's own origin.
intended_behavior: Timing metrics should be available only to the same-origin client application for RUM/performance monitoring.

trace.scope: onSend hook registered on all routes
trace.description: Hook fires on every response before it is sent to the client
Wildcard Timing-Allow-Origin header allows any cross-origin page to read timing via performance.getEntriesByType('resource')

evidence.description: reply.header('Timing-Allow-Origin', '*') — unconditional wildcard on all responses

conditions.description: Victim must visit an attacker-controlled page in the same browser session where they have made API requests
Browser must support and expose Resource Timing API (all modern browsers do)

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker who can serve a page to the victim (cross-origin attacker)
instructions: Host a page at an arbitrary origin
Make a cross-origin fetch to the booking API with a candidate ticket ID
Read performance.getEntriesByType('resource') — Timing-Allow-Origin: * allows this
Compare response time: faster response (~1ms) for non-existent tickets vs longer (~5-10ms) for existing tickets reveals existence
execution.observed_result: Cross-origin pages can read precise API response timing, enabling booking existence oracles and admin session probes.

remediation.strategy: Remove the Timing-Allow-Origin header entirely. Core Web Vitals RUM and performance monitoring do not require cross-origin timing access — same-origin requests are measurable without this header. If cross-origin RUM is specifically needed, restrict to the application's own domain.

likelihood.reason: Requires victim to visit attacker-controlled page. Ticket ID enumeration is also limited by the rate limiter. Practical exploitation requires chaining with other information.

impact.reason: Reveals existence of booking records and potentially session validity. Does not directly expose PII or enable privilege escalation.

confidence.reason: Timing-Allow-Origin: * is directly observable in source. The timing oracle mechanism is well-documented W3C browser behavior.

title: docker-compose.yml enables ALLOW_TEST_AUTH without NODE_ENV=production — test auth backdoor active in container deployments
description: docker-compose.yml sets ALLOW_TEST_AUTH: true but does not set NODE_ENV=production. The env.ts production check only blocks ALLOW_TEST_AUTH when NODE_ENV is exactly 'production'. Any developer running docker-compose in staging receives a server where Authorization: Bearer test-super_admin grants full super_admin access to all admin routes including refunds and booking transitions.
root_cause: docker-compose.yml:10 sets ALLOW_TEST_AUTH: true for container convenience, but the missing NODE_ENV=production means env.ts's production guard never fires and the backdoor remains active.
intended_behavior: ALLOW_TEST_AUTH should be confined strictly to test harnesses (vitest.config.ts, tests/helpers.ts). Container deployments should not have this backdoor.

trace.description: Sets test auth backdoor active for all containers built from this compose file
When ALLOW_TEST_AUTH is true, any token starting with 'test-' grants the corresponding role without JWT verification
With test-super_admin token, attacker passes requireRole check and can issue refunds for any booking

evidence.description: ALLOW_TEST_AUTH: true in the docker-compose environment block
if (env.ALLOW_TEST_AUTH) missing.push('ALLOW_TEST_AUTH must be false in production') — only checked when NODE_ENV=production, which docker-compose does not set

conditions.description: Server must be running with docker-compose.yml (or a configuration derived from it) without overriding NODE_ENV=production
Attacker must be able to reach the deployed backend API

execution.attacker_perspective: Any unauthenticated HTTP caller with network access to the backend
instructions: Send any request to a protected admin endpoint with header: Authorization: Bearer test-super_admin
Example: POST /api/v1/ops/admin/refunds with {bookingId: '<any>', reason: 'test refund', idempotencyKey: 'idem-1'}
Observe that the request succeeds with 201 — no real credentials required
execution.observed_result: Full super_admin access granted. All admin routes accessible including bookings list, refund initiation, booking status transitions, and audit logs.

remediation.strategy: Remove ALLOW_TEST_AUTH from docker-compose.yml entirely. This variable belongs only in vitest.config.ts and tests/helpers.ts. Add a CI check (grep in pre-commit or CI pipeline) that fails if ALLOW_TEST_AUTH=true appears in docker-compose.yml.

code_changes.fixed_code:
# Remove: ALLOW_TEST_AUTH: "true"
# Add to production env validation: also check if ALLOW_TEST_AUTH is truthy regardless of NODE_ENV when DATABASE_URL is set

likelihood.reason: Requires docker-compose to be used in a deployed environment. Developers working locally are the primary risk. The commit history suggests docker-compose is used for local dev, but staging accidents are plausible.

impact.reason: Grants complete super_admin access — can read all bookings, customer PII, issue refunds draining business funds, and transition bookings to arbitrary states.

confidence.reason: Both docker-compose.yml and authGuard.ts are in source. The conditional logic in env.ts:82 is directly traceable — the guard fires only in NODE_ENV=production.

title: Hardcoded fallback webhook secrets allow forged payment capture events
description: app.ts creates PayPal and Card payment adapters with hardcoded fallback HMAC secrets ('whsec_paypal_test', 'whsec_card_test') when the corresponding env vars are not set. These strings are in the public source repository. An attacker with source access can forge valid HMAC signatures for any webhook payload and force bookings to paid_confirmed without real payment.
root_cause: app.ts:221 and app.ts:228 use the || operator to fall back to known string literals when PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CARD_WEBHOOK_SECRET are not configured. These literals are public knowledge.
intended_behavior: Webhook signature verification must use secrets that are not known to attackers. Missing secrets should cause a startup failure, not a silent fallback.

trace.description: Unauthenticated webhook entry point for paypal and card providers
When PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty, adapter uses known fallback string as HMAC key
Successful webhook verification triggers booking status update to paid_confirmed without real payment

evidence.description: webhookSecret: env.PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET || 'whsec_paypal_test' — literal fallback in public source
webhookSecret: env.CARD_WEBHOOK_SECRET || 'whsec_card_test' — literal fallback in public source

conditions.description: Server must be running without PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET or CARD_WEBHOOK_SECRET environment variables configured
A booking with a valid providerOrderId must exist in the system for the webhook to update booking status

execution.attacker_perspective: Any HTTP caller who knows the fallback HMAC secret (available in source code)
payloads: HMAC-SHA256('whsec_paypal_test', <forged_payload>) as the webhook signature header
instructions: Craft a JSON payload mimicking a PayPal payment.captured event with a known providerOrderId
Sign it with HMAC-SHA256 using key 'whsec_paypal_test'
POST to /api/v1/payments/webhooks/paypal with the signature in the appropriate header
Observe: verifyWebhook returns true, booking is marked paid_confirmed without real payment
execution.observed_result: Forged webhook accepted as legitimate. Booking transitions to paid_confirmed, notifications sent, promo redemption count incremented — all without actual payment.

remediation.strategy: Remove all fallback string literals for webhook secrets. Throw an error at startup if any configured payment provider is missing its webhook secret. Add PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CARD_WEBHOOK_SECRET to the production required fields check in env.ts.

likelihood.reason: Requires server to be misconfigured (missing webhook secrets) AND attacker to know fallback strings (public in source). Partial deployment misconfiguration is plausible.

impact.reason: Allows forging payment confirmation for any booking — business revenue loss and potential service abuse.

confidence.reason: Source directly shows the fallback strings. HMAC verification path is traceable from webhook endpoint through payment.service.ts:197.

title: Client-supplied distanceKm accepted in booking draft and affects server fare calculation
description: The customer-facing booking schema accepts distanceKm as a numeric input (1 to 5000). This value flows directly into the fare engine. For routes not in the catalogue (estimated routes), the client-supplied distance is used without a server-side floor. A customer can artificially lower their fare by submitting a small distanceKm.
root_cause: booking.schema.ts:54 includes distanceKm as a customer-supplied field. The fare engine uses Math.max(input.distanceKm, route.km) only for catalogue routes; for uncatalogued routes, route.km is estimated and may itself be inaccurate.
intended_behavior: Fares should be server-authoritative. Client-supplied monetary and distance inputs that affect fare should not be trusted.

trace.description: Customer supplies distanceKm between 0.001 and 5000 in the POST /api/v1/bookings/draft body
Customer-supplied distanceKm passed directly to fare engine
For uncatalogued routes, estimatedKm is used as route.km. Math.max(input.distanceKm, route.km) may still favor client value if estimated distance is also small.

evidence.description: distanceKm: z.number().positive().max(5000).finite() — accepts any positive value up to 5000
const billedDistance = Math.max(input.distanceKm, route.km) — protects only catalogue routes with known km

conditions.description: Route must not be in the ROUTES catalogue with a known km value, or the catalogue km must be smaller than the actual route distance

execution.attacker_perspective: Customer who knows an unlisted route pair
instructions: Submit a booking draft with origin/destination not in the fare catalogue
Set distanceKm: 1 (minimum positive value above schema floor)
Observe: fare is calculated at 1km — sedan: Math.max(2200, 1*10) = 2200 INR regardless of actual route distance
Compare with legitimate 500km route: sedan should be Math.max(2200, 500*10) = 5000 INR
execution.observed_result: Customer receives the minimum fare (₹2200 sedan) for any unlisted route regardless of actual distance.

remediation.strategy: Remove distanceKm from the customer-facing booking schema. Derive distance server-side using findRoute(originName, destinationName).km from the fare engine. If dynamic distance is needed, require an origin/destination coordinate pair and compute distance server-side.

code_changes.fixed_code:
// Remove: distanceKm: z.number().positive().max(5000).finite()
// The service should derive distanceKm from findRoute(originName, destinationName).km

likelihood.reason: Any customer who reads the API schema or inspects network traffic can discover and exploit this. No special knowledge required.

impact.reason: Business revenue impact — customers pay minimum fare regardless of actual distance for unlisted routes. Does not affect data integrity or user safety.

confidence.reason: Source path from booking schema through booking service into fare engine is directly traceable. The Math.max guard only applies for known routes.

title: Admin development fallback grants super_admin role with hardcoded token when Supabase is not configured
description: admin/src/lib/auth.ts falls back to a mode where any syntactically valid email and any 6-char password authenticate as super_admin with token 'test-super_admin', when VITE_SUPABASE_URL or VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY is absent from the build. This token is then accepted by the backend if ALLOW_TEST_AUTH is also enabled (SEC-003).
root_cause: auth.ts:27 branches on env.SUPABASE_URL && env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY. When either is missing, the code falls through to a development fallback that issues a hardcoded super_admin token.
intended_behavior: The admin panel must require real Supabase credentials for all environments. No credential fallback should exist.

trace.description: Attacker or unauthorized user submits any email + 6-char password
When Supabase not configured, skips real auth and falls through to development fallback
Hardcoded super_admin token written to localStorage['skb-admin-session']; used as Bearer token for all subsequent API calls

evidence.description: token: 'test-super_admin' — hardcoded token in development fallback
if (env.SUPABASE_URL && env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY) — fallback triggers when either is missing

conditions.description: Admin app must be built/served without VITE_SUPABASE_URL or VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY set
Backend must have ALLOW_TEST_AUTH enabled for the token to grant backend access (see SEC-003)

execution.attacker_perspective: Any user with access to the admin login page when Supabase is not configured
instructions: Access admin panel URL when VITE_SUPABASE_URL is not set in the build
Enter any valid-format email and any 6+ char password
Observe: loginWithCredentials returns adminUser with role super_admin and token test-super_admin
Admin panel is now accessible with full super_admin session
execution.observed_result: Complete admin access granted without credentials. If backend also has ALLOW_TEST_AUTH, backend API calls succeed as super_admin.

remediation.strategy: Remove the development fallback entirely. Require VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY to be set for all builds — add a Vite plugin or env check that throws at build time if they are missing. For local development, use Supabase local/docker.

likelihood.reason: Requires admin panel to be deployed without Supabase configuration. Plausible in staging or local container environments.

impact.reason: Grants admin panel UI access. Business impact depends on whether backend ALLOW_TEST_AUTH is also enabled (SEC-003 chain).

confidence.reason: Source is directly observable. The conditional branch at auth.ts:27 and the fallback token at auth.ts:81 are unambiguous.

title: Duplicate booking guard fetches only 20 most recent bookings — bypassable under concurrent load
description: The duplicate booking prevention check fetches the 20 most recent bookings globally and searches for a matching phone/route/pickup within the last 5 minutes. If more than 20 bookings exist in that window (high load or coordinated attack), the check fails to detect the duplicate.
root_cause: booking.service.ts:71 uses pageSize: 20 for the dedup scan. This is a global page scan rather than a targeted DB query by phone number and time window.
intended_behavior: Duplicate booking detection should reliably prevent the same customer from creating multiple identical bookings within 5 minutes.

trace.description: Customer submits booking draft — rate limited to 30/min per IP
Fetches 20 most recent bookings globally — not filtered by phone or time window at DB level
If duplicate not in first 20 results, check passes and second booking is created

evidence.description: deps.db.bookings.list({ page: 1, pageSize: 20 }) — global scan limited to 20 most recent

conditions.description: More than 20 bookings must be created globally within the 5-minute dedup window for the bypass to work

execution.attacker_perspective: Customer or script creating duplicate bookings
payloads: 21+ concurrent POST /api/v1/bookings/draft requests (may require multiple IPs due to 30/min rate limit)
instructions: Submit 20 bookings from other phone numbers to fill the page-20 scan result
Submit the 21st booking with the same phone/route as a prior booking
Duplicate check scans the first 20 results — prior matching booking not found
Duplicate booking created without conflict error
execution.observed_result: Duplicate booking created for the same customer phone/route/time without detection.

remediation.strategy: Replace the global page scan with a targeted query: add a bookings.findRecentByPhone(phone, since) method that queries by customer_phone and created_at >= window. For PostgreSQL, add an index on (customer_phone, created_at).

likelihood.reason: Requires high booking volume or coordinated load. The 30/min per-IP rate limit makes single-IP exploitation difficult. Requires knowledge of this implementation detail.

impact.reason: Creates duplicate booking records — operator confusion and extra support overhead, but does not affect payment or user data integrity directly.

confidence.reason: The pageSize:20 limit is directly observable in source. The dedup logic scanning a limited global list rather than a targeted query is clearly insufficient.

title: phoneLast4 in public booking response reduces phone enumeration search space
description: The public booking GET endpoint returns phoneLast4 (last 4 digits of the customer's phone) to any caller who can access the booking via guestAccessToken or phone verification. The AGR-YYYYMMDD-NNNN ticket ID format has only 10,000 permutations per day. An enumerator who discovers a valid ticket ID and guesses the last 4 phone digits can retrieve the customer's name and masked contact info.
root_cause: booking.service.ts:229 includes phoneLast4: last4(booking.customerPhone) in the projectBooking response without verifying this is necessary for any legitimate frontend use case.
intended_behavior: PII should be minimized in public API responses. phoneLast4 serves no verified customer use case in the response body.

trace.description: Enumerator discovers valid ticket ID by iterating AGR-YYYYMMDD-0001 through 9999
Access granted with matching guestAccessToken OR matching phone number
phoneLast4 returned to any authenticated caller — leaks partial phone, reduces brute-force space from 10^10 to 10^4

evidence.description: phoneLast4: last4(booking.customerPhone) — returned to all callers who pass guestAccessToken or phone check
return `AGR-${ymd}-${suffix}` where suffix is randomInt(0, 10000) — 10,000 permutations per date

conditions.description: Attacker must know approximate booking date to enumerate ticket IDs (10,000 per day)
Access requires guestAccessToken OR correct phone number — phoneLast4 reduces the phone search space to 10^4 combinations

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker who knows or can guess a booking date
instructions: Enumerate ticket IDs for a known date: AGR-20260916-0001 through AGR-20260916-9999
For each valid ticket, attempt access with any guestAccessToken — access fails but existence can be confirmed by response type
For confirmed-existing tickets, the phoneLast4 in the response after gaining access reveals partial phone
Use phoneLast4 to narrow phone enumeration from 10^10 to 10^4 possibilities
execution.observed_result: phoneLast4 returned in booking response reduces the search space for phone-based booking access by 6 orders of magnitude.

remediation.strategy: Remove phoneLast4 from the projectBooking response. The frontend should not need partial phone information to display the booking confirmation. If identification is needed, use the masked phone (already included) or the ticket ID.

likelihood.reason: Requires knowledge of approximate booking date and access to an existing booking token. Ticket ID enumeration is limited by rate limits.

impact.reason: Reveals partial PII (last 4 phone digits). Does not enable account takeover or payment manipulation directly.

confidence.reason: phoneLast4 in projectBooking is directly observable. The ticket ID space calculation is source-grounded in ids.ts:17.

title: CORS allows requests with no Origin header in production — Origin not a trust signal but worth confirming
description: app.ts:94-110 calls cb(null, true) for requests with no Origin header in both development and production. This means all server-to-server callers (curl, webhook providers, mobile apps) are not subject to CORS origin restrictions.
claimed_root_cause: CORS callback at app.ts:96-103 accepts missing-Origin requests without restriction in production. If any middleware relied on Origin as a trust signal, this would be a bypass. Static analysis of current source shows authentication uses JWT and HMAC — not Origin — so this may be benign.

trace.description: CORS decision point for all incoming requests

trace.scope: cb(null, true) — allow request without Origin
trace.description: All requests without Origin header allowed unconditionally in production

evidence.description: if (!origin) { if (env.NODE_ENV === 'production') { cb(null, true); return; } ... } — both branches call cb(null, true)

blockers: CORS is a browser security primitive, not an API authentication mechanism. Non-browser callers (curl, mobile, webhook providers) never send Origin headers. If authentication is handled by JWT and HMAC (which it is in this codebase), then accepting no-Origin requests is standard and correct. Validation needed: confirm that no route handler or middleware reads request.headers.origin as a trust signal.

validation_plan.local: Search codebase for any reference to request.headers.origin or req.headers.origin used in a security decision. If none found, this is not a vulnerability.
validation_plan.deployment: Confirm the deployed API does not rely on CDN or proxy-level Origin enforcement that would make this a more significant gap.

title: Razorpay checkout stores provider-echoed amount rather than server-computed amount
description: razorpay.ts:74 stores body.amount (echoed from Razorpay API response) as the payment record's amountMinor. The webhook reconciliation then compares event.amountMinor === payment.amountMinor — both sides are Razorpay-reported rather than comparing against the originally server-computed amount.
claimed_root_cause: razorpay.ts:74 uses body.amount from Razorpay's order creation response instead of asserting it equals command.amountMinor before storing.

trace.scope: createCheckout — sends amount: command.amountMinor to Razorpay
trace.description: Server sends the computed amountMinor to Razorpay order creation API
Stores Razorpay-echoed amount rather than the sent amount
Webhook check compares two Razorpay-sourced values — if Razorpay misbehaves, server-computed amount is not in the comparison

evidence.description: amountMinor: body.amount — uses provider-echoed value without asserting equality with sent amount

blockers: Razorpay's order API is documented to echo exactly the amount sent. A discrepancy would indicate a provider bug, not an attacker-controlled path. The risk is theoretical — an attacker cannot influence Razorpay's API response for a server-to-server call. Validation needed: add an assertion body.amount === command.amountMinor and confirm Razorpay never rounds or modifies the amount.

validation_plan.local: Add assertion: if (body.amount !== command.amountMinor) throw new Error('Razorpay returned unexpected amount'); Test with the Razorpay test API to confirm echoed amount equals sent amount.
validation_plan.deployment: Monitor Razorpay webhook events for amount discrepancies using the existing needs_review reconciliation path.
